clue.text: Weak man, penniless, runs to uncle

parts.note: in chess the pawn is the weakest man on the board
penniless means broke
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A feeble, broke man hurries off to his uncle for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for the pawnshop keeper, from whom the poor borrowed against goods; the surface makes it a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls the lender who takes goods as security 'uncle', a jocular name for that tradesman.

clue.text: Diamond-shaped tablet is a success

definitions.meaning: in heraldry a hatchment is a lozenge-shaped panel bearing a dead person's arms, once known by another name
a success is a feat or accomplishment

explanation.walkthrough: The hatchment, a diamond-shaped board showing the arms of someone recently dead, was formerly called by this name. 'is a' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic funeral panel was once called this; it also means an accomplishment or feat.

clue.text: Paper is picked up here in the street

definitions.text: Paper is picked up here in the street

parts.words: Paper is picked up here in the street
parts.note: a newspaper is bought at a kiosk on the pavement

explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests litter collected from the road; it means buying a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A street kiosk or stall selling newspapers and magazines is this.

clue.text: Clergyman protecting a source of power

indicators.note: protecting means the clergyman's title wraps round the letter a

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar shields a source of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of power' sounds spiritual next to the clergyman; it is a nuclear reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor generates energy for power stations, so it is a source of power.

clue.text: Don't go to pot — stay on the straight and narrow

definitions.text: Don't go to pot — stay on the straight and narrow

parts.words: Don't go to pot — stay on the straight and narrow
parts.note: pot and grass are slang for cannabis, and the familiar sign tells walkers to keep to the path

explanation.walkthrough: The notice on lawns tells people to stick to paths; 'pot' and 'grass' both mean cannabis, so it is also advice to avoid drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The park notice telling walkers not to tread on the lawn also reads as advice to avoid cannabis.

clue.text: Do a turn badly in the circular hall

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of do a turn are performed in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone performs poorly while dancing in a round room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' looks like a comment on a performance; it signals an anagram of DO A TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building or room, often domed.

clue.text: Card game turned into habit

indicators.note: turned tells us the name of the card game is read backwards

parts.note: brag is a British card game, a forerunner of poker

explanation.surface: A game of cards turned into a regular habit.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAG is a British card game related to poker. 'Habit' means clothing here, as in a monk's habit, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a distinctive dress, such as a nun's, so it means clothing or costume.

clue.text: Cause resentment, missing opening of low-down joint

indicators.note: missing opening means the word for causing resentment loses its first letter

parts.note: to rankle is to cause lasting resentment

explanation.surface: A seedy bar causes ill feeling by not opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low-down joint' suggests a disreputable bar; it is the joint lowest down the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between leg and foot, the lowest major joint of the body.

clue.text: Split right in the middle of chest

indicators.note: in the middle of puts the letter for right inside the word for chest

parts.note: a bust is the chest

explanation.surface: A split right across the middle of a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst is to break open or split apart suddenly.

clue.text: Display, for example, a musical box

parts.note: a musical is an example of a show
a case is a box or container

explanation.surface: Something to put on view, such as a music box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' tells us a musical is one kind of show; 'musical box' in the surface is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a glass cabinet or setting for putting things on view, so it is a display.

clue.text: Gypsy's fiddle

definitions.meaning: a travelling mender of pots, a term used for travellers
to fiddle with something is to ... with it

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling pot-mender was called by this name; as a verb it means to meddle or adjust idly.

clue.text: Double rm.?

parts.note: rm. is short for room; this one doubles as a bedroom and a sitting room

explanation.walkthrough: A 'double room' in a hotel has a bed for two; here the room does double duty, being both bedroom and sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: A single rented room serving for both sleeping and living is a bed-sitting room, shortened.

clue.text: Deck soldiers used to call no trumps

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to call someone something is to name them
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: Card players who served in the army would call no trumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a pack of cards amid all the bridge talk, but it is a verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a hall is to decorate or adorn it, which is the verb sense here.

clue.text: Reading between the lines, it's relatively small

definitions.text: Reading between the lines, it's relatively small

parts.words: Reading between the lines, it's relatively small
parts.note: the lines are railway lines, and the measure between the rails is a gauge that is small on some railways

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading between the lines' sounds like inferring a hidden meaning; it is a measurement between rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway whose rails are set closer together than standard track is said to have this.

clue.text: Old character sounding like Wackford Squeers

indicators.note: sounding like says we want a word said the same as a description of Squeers

parts.note: the brutal schoolmaster in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby, who beat his pupils

explanation.surface: An old figure who sounds like a Dickens villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeers runs Dotheboys Hall in Nicholas Nickleby and thrashes the boys, so he is a beater; in non-rhotic speech that sounds like the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the ancient Greek alphabet is a character, in the sense of a written letter.

clue.text: Unmanageable ringleader in works is behind the engineers

indicators.note: is behind puts the next part after the engineers in the answer

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: in places the ring's first letter inside the word for a works

parts.note: a works is a factory
the leader, or first letter, of ring is R

explanation.surface: A troublesome ringleader in the factory is the one behind the engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' is read as the leading letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory describes someone stubbornly resistant to control, so unmanageable.

clue.text: Rearrest university crook who's in charge of funds?

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of shape, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: Arrest again the university swindler who ran the finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal, but it signals an anagram of REARREST plus U.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the official who manages an organisation's money.

clue.text: Editorials with informed guidance

parts.note: a newspaper's leaders are its editorials
hip means well informed, in the know

explanation.definitionFit: Leadership is the act of directing or guiding others, so it means guidance.

clue.text: Sat on throne, but came down to speak

indicators.note: to speak means the word for coming down is heard rather than written

parts.note: rain coming down means it rained

explanation.surface: A king sat on his throne, then came down to address the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came down' sounds like stepping off the throne; it is weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who sat on the throne held royal power and ruled.

clue.text: Alter the sequence for each non-speaking actor

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
a mute is an actor with no lines

explanation.surface: Change the order for every silent performer.
explanation.definitionFit: To permute is to rearrange items into a different order.

clue.text: English-style college

parts.note: ton means fashionable style, as in high society

explanation.surface: A college built in the English manner.
explanation.walkthrough: TON is a dated word for fashion or chic, as in 'the ton' of Regency society. Eton is the famous school near Windsor, formally Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous public school near Windsor is formally named Eton College.

clue.text: Dental filling breaking off

definitions.meaning: a tooth filling is also called a ... in British usage

explanation.definitionFit: Dentists once called a tooth filling by this name; as a verb form it means ceasing or halting.

clue.text: Taking part in Swiss ambassador's dance

indicators.note: Taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Joining in the Swiss envoy's dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian ballroom and carnival dance.

clue.text: Tender proposal

definitions.meaning: to tender something is to put it forward
a proposal is something put forward for acceptance

explanation.definitionFit: To put something forward, or the thing put forward for acceptance, is this word.

clue.text: Singer ordered to stop performing work

indicators.note: ordered here means put in a new order, so the letters of the clue word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer is told to cease performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as commanded in the surface but signals that SINGER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit one's job or post is to give up working there.

clue.text: Makin' a mess of spongy cake

definitions.meaning: to muff is to botch; with the final g dropped, as in makin', botching becomes this word
a small spongy cake or bread roll

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Makin'' signals the dropped g, so the botching sense loses its last letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: A small light baked cake, eaten toasted or as a cupcake, is this item; muffing with the g dropped means bungling.

clue.text: In which the members of a school are clearly on display

definitions.text: In which the members of a school are clearly on display

parts.words: In which the members of a school are clearly on display
parts.note: the school is a school of fish, seen through glass walls

explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests pupils on show; it is a shoal of fish, and 'clearly' points to the glass tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tank or building where fish are kept on view is this.

clue.text: Divine measure in which Gray's elegy was written

definitions.text: Divine measure in which Gray's elegy was written

parts.words: Divine measure in which Gray's elegy was written
parts.note: Gray's poem is Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.walkthrough: 'measure' sounds like a poetic metre, but it is a unit of land; 'God's acre' is a churchyard, the setting of Thomas Gray's famous elegy.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area is a measure, and God's acre is an old name for a churchyard.

clue.text: Cast down, then raised anew

indicators.note: anew means the letters of the words before it are made over in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Thrown down, then lifted up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised anew' looks like the opposite of 'Cast down'; in fact 'anew' rearranges THEN RAISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cast down is to be dejected, and to make someone lose heart is the verb here.
